title: Write Characterization Tests for Existing Code
objective: Add automated tests that pin down what an existing, untested Python function or small module actually does today, including at least one surprising or edge-case behavior.
whyThisMatters: Most professional test-writing isn't test-driven development against a blank page — it's adding a safety net to code that already exists and has no tests. Characterization tests let you change that code later without breaking behavior you didn't know something depended on.
evidence: The test file(s), committed with a message describing what they characterize
Console output of the test run showing all tests passing
A short note identifying the surprising or edge-case behavior found
AI disclosure entry if AI helped generate test cases
acceptanceCriteria: At least 6 test cases exist, covering normal input, at least one edge case, and at least one invalid or unexpected input.
All tests pass against the existing code, unmodified.
A comment or accompanying note names at least one place where the code's current behavior looks surprising or wrong, without fixing it.
Tests run with a single documented command, and that command's output is included in the evidence.
